author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Eutelsat has placed a €1 billion order with Airbus for 229 low-Earth-orbit satellites, expanding a replenishment plan intended to keep its OneWeb broadband network operating through 2034. The new spacecraft add to 440 satellites ordered in 2024 and 2025.

OneWeb operates more than 600 satellites and competes with SpaceX’s much larger Starlink network, which has more than 11,000. Eutelsat’s constellation flies at a higher orbit and is focused heavily on business, government and telecommunications customers rather than relying mainly on direct consumer service.

The order is designed to maintain service continuity until Europe’s planned IRIS² secure communications network becomes available near the end of the decade. Eutelsat has also booked two launches on Europe’s Ariane rocket for 2027 and 2028, Reuters reported.

For Europe, the purchase has strategic as well as commercial significance. OneWeb is the region’s primary operational low-orbit alternative to Starlink, and keeping the network refreshed reduces the risk of a capacity gap before IRIS² is deployed. The long timetable also underscores how satellite internet systems require continual replacement: spacecraft have finite operating lives, while demand, cybersecurity requirements and launch schedules keep changing.
dek: The €1 billion Airbus order will replenish the low-orbit constellation as Europe’s Starlink rival bridges toward the planned IRIS² system.
headline: Eutelsat orders 229 satellites to extend OneWeb network through 2034
